triggers.rationale: Gave back 15% from the high. This is a question, not a sale: is the reason we bought still true? If yes, hold and raise the floor under real structure (the 20-day low, the breakout level). If partly, trim. Sell only if you can name what broke in the business.
Gave back 25% from the high — the catastrophe line for a multi-year hold. The review at 15% should have acted long before this; if we are here, protect the capital.
Below the 200-day — the long trend is in question. Review the business, not the chart.
Up 15% from entry — re-underwrite at the new price and raise the floor under real structure (DAV-279 ruling).
Down 15% from entry — decide hold-vs-cut deliberately, before the stop decides (DAV-279 ruling).
Down 7% in a day — evaluate a pullback-add ONLY if the drop is market/sector-wide with the thesis intact. A company-specific drop is thesis damage: do not add — hold, trim, or exit. Approval-gated.
Up 7% in a day — strength on a held name. Evaluate pressing the winner (add + raise target/stop) if the move is thesis-confirming, not an exhaustion spike. Approval-gated.
Look at this every 7 days, counting from the last real review.
Reports within 3 days — decide before the print: hold through it, trim, or wait to add. Size for the gap.
Reported a beat — re-underwrite. A clean beat-and-raise earns a higher target; a beat the stock sold on means the market wanted more.
Reported a miss — is the thesis wrong, or early? Decide deliberately before the stop decides for us.

Filed something material with the SEC — read the filing first; the code says what happened, not whether it's good. A restatement or bankruptcy breaks the numbers; an officer leaving or a deal can change the story.

thesisBefore.coreBelief: VST compounds toward $210 over 18–24 months as Helix preferred-power status and long-dated AWS/Meta nuclear PPAs convert AI datacenter load growth into contracted EBITDA that lifts the 2027 baseline of $7.4–$7.8B (ex-Cogentrix/Meta) while multiple re-rates from ~8x toward 10–11x as earnings visibility improves.
keyAssumptions: Vistra's 2026 adjusted EBITDA lands at or above the $7.2B midpoint of the $6.8–$7.6B guidance range, validating management's reaffirmation despite ERCOT softness
Helix Digital Infrastructure breaks ground on at least one AI datacenter site by mid-2027, with Vistra contracted power volume becoming quantifiable in public guidance

ERCOT forward power prices do not sustain a structural decline below current softened levels — i.e., load growth of 4–6% annually through 2030 absorbs incremental supply without prolonged price compression
invalidationConds: Two consecutive formal guidance cuts to the adjusted EBITDA range — not a single quarter miss but management explicitly lowering the annual band twice in succession, signaling structural demand erosion rather than timing
Helix Digital Infrastructure cancels or materially restructures such that Vistra is no longer the preferred power provider, eliminating the contracted AI-load thesis and the $1B investment value

VST breaks and closes below the 52-week low of $132.66 on material volume AND management issues a negative business update within 30 days, confirming the technical break reflects fundamental deterioration rather than sentiment overshoot
CFO Kristopher Moldovan departure within 12 months, given his centrality to the capital allocation and leverage management narrative through the Cogentrix integration
thesisBefore.variantView: Consensus treats VST as a regulated-adjacent utility; I believe the Helix JV structurally transforms it into a contracted hyperscaler power platform, locking in multi-year load growth that is not yet in sell-side EBITDA models.
thesisBefore.convictionRationale: The EBITDA story is real — Q2 up 30% YoY, 2026 guidance intact, 2027 baseline before major upsides already implies ~$200+ stock — but I cannot call this HIGH conviction until Helix revenue shows up in actual guidance, ERCOT forwards stabilize, and the 25% EPS beat rate repairs. MEDIUM is honest here.

submit.conviction_rationale: The strategic thesis is intact and the Helix preferred-power anchor is now corroborated by Samsung's $1B commitment alongside NVIDIA, KKR, and KIA. The business is growing EBITDA 30%+ YoY. But two consecutive massive EPS misses, ERCOT spot at $30/MWh with no near-term catalyst for repricing, a broken chart with all moving averages declining, and the stock trading 36% below its 52-week high make this MEDIUM — the thesis is right but the market is right to wait for proof. I do not have HIGH conviction until I see a 50-day reclaim on volume and a Q3 print that holds or raises the 2026 guidance midpoint.
submit.core_belief: VST compounds toward $210 over 18–24 months as Vistra's preferred-power status inside the now-$11B+ Helix platform and contracted PJM/ISO-NE capacity from the pending Cogentrix close convert AI datacenter load growth into durable contracted EBITDA, lifting the 2027–2028 earnings baseline while the market re-rates from ~10x toward 11–12x as ERCOT softness resolves and guidance visibility improves.
invalidation_conditions: Two consecutive full-year EBITDA guidance cuts (not quarterly misses — a cut to the annual range itself for 2026 or 2027 that narrows the bottom of the band below $6.4B).
Cogentrix acquisition fails to close or FERC approval is reversed, eliminating the PJM/ISO-NE diversification thesis.

CFO departure or a capital-allocation pivot away from growth (e.g., suspension of the buyback program combined with a leverage covenant breach) that signals balance sheet stress rather than strategic investment.
Helix relationship deteriorates — Vistra loses preferred-power status or Helix publicly moves its power sourcing to a competing generator.
key_assumptions: ERCOT load growth inflects in 2027–2028 as data-center interconnections materialize, validating management's 4–6% annual growth forecast and tightening reserve margins from today's loose levels.
The Cogentrix acquisition closes in late 2026 (FERC approved August 2026) and adds at minimum the originally guided PJM/ISO-NE EBITDA contribution at the time of the deal announcement.

Vistra's preferred-power role inside Helix produces at least one publicly announced commercial arrangement (contracted MW or PPA) within 12 months that demonstrates the financial mechanism, not just the strategic relationship.
